questions.prompt: What is an optional in Swift, and why does Swift require optionals to represent missing values? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Defines an optional as a type that holds either a real value or nil
Explains that normal types in Swift can never be nil
Mentions that optionals help prevent null pointer crashes by requiring handling at compile time

questions.modelAnswer: An optional in Swift is a type that holds either a real value or nil. Normal types in Swift can never hold nil. This design helps prevent null pointer crashes because the compiler makes you handle missing values before using them.

sources.title: The Swift Programming Language: The Basics (Optionals)

questions.prompt: Compare if let and guard let for unwrapping optionals in Swift. When should you choose each? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that if let binds the unwrapped constant only inside the if block
Explains that guard let keeps the unwrapped constant in the outer block and requires an early exit
Explains when to choose each (guard let for early exits to avoid nesting; if let for simple branches)

questions.modelAnswer: Both if let and guard let unwrap optionals safely. With if let, the unwrapped constant works only inside the if block. With guard let, the else block must leave the scope, and the unwrapped value stays available in the rest of the block. Choose guard let for early exits to keep code flat, and if let for simple conditional branches.

sources.title: The Swift Programming Language: The Basics (Optionals)

questions.prompt: How does the nil-coalescing operator (??) work, and what advantages does it offer over forced unwrapping? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that ?? returns the wrapped value if present, or a default value if nil
Explains that it gives a non-optional value safely without crashing
Contrasts this with forced unwrapping (!) which crashes right away on nil

questions.modelAnswer: The nil-coalescing operator ?? gives the wrapped value if the optional has one, or a default value if it is nil. Unlike forced unwrapping with !, which crashes right away on nil, ?? is always safe. It lets your app handle missing data cleanly and gives you a plain non-optional value.

questions.prompt: Why is forced unwrapping with ! risky in app code, and what should you use instead? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: States that forced unwrapping causes a fatal runtime crash if the value is nil
Explains that it stops the compiler from making you handle nil first
Recommends safe alternatives like if let, guard let, or ??

questions.modelAnswer: Forced unwrapping with ! stops the compiler from making you handle nil first. If the optional holds nil at runtime, the app crashes with a fatal error. In app code, use safe unwrapping like if let, guard let, or ?? instead.
